review_notes: Read the whole file and its two downstream uses (Fibrant/CofibrantObjectHomotopy). No simp attributes exist in the file. quotient_iff is the canonical characterisation of the new predicate on images of functor maps, but it is only used through `apply`, with a manual `simp only` or `simpa only` step around it. The finding is a modest suggestion. I did not check whether the attribute would conflict with other simp lemmas, and I did not run Lean. HasQuotient.iff_of_eqvGen and eq_inverseImage_quotientFunctor are poor simp candidates, so I left them alone.

findings.excerpt:
lemma quotient_iff {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    W.quotient homRel ((Quotient.functor homRel).map f) ↔ W f := by
findings.problem: This is the canonical reduction of the induced predicate `W.quotient homRel` on an image `(Quotient.functor homRel).map f` back to `W f`. The LHS is a head symbol applied to a functor-map pattern, and the RHS is strictly simpler, so it would be a safe simp lemma. It is not tagged `@[simp]`. Downstream code therefore has to apply it by hand. In FibrantObjectHomotopy, `weakEquivalence_toHoCat_map_iff` is proved by `simp only [weakEquivalence_iff]` followed by `apply MorphismProperty.quotient_iff`. The CofibrantObjectHomotopy proof does the same. A `simpa only [..., weakEquivalence_toHoCat_map_iff]` is then needed in `toHoCatLocalizerMorphism`, to rewrite the quotient predicate by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `quotient_iff` as `@[simp]`, so that `(W.quotient homRel) ((Quotient.functor homRel).map f)` normalises to `W f`. Do this only if the instance arguments `[W.HasQuotient homRel]` unify without trouble. The two `apply MorphismProperty.quotient_iff` steps downstream could then become `simp`. Leave `eq_inverseImage_quotientFunctor` non-simp, because its LHS is the bare variable `W` and it would loop.
findings.benefit: Goals mentioning `W.quotient homRel` applied to a quotient-functor image would be simplified automatically to `W f`. Users of the quotient construction would not need to remember the lemma name.
